move: threshold level sweeps footage between ink and paper, accent band rides the edge
how: A 640x360 canvas repaints a procedural sunset each frame (panning 60px on a sine over the loop) then every pixel's luminance is compared to a threshold level that sweeps 0.18 to 0.82 on a full sine over the 4s loop; pixels resolve to near-black ink or warm paper through a soft edge whose width tightens (0.02 to 0.08) at the extremes, so the picture breathes from mostly-ink to mostly-paper and back. A thin luminance band just above the level is painted orange-red, giving a sweeping accent contour. Over the canvas, a 'Threshold 50%' readout with a bar (width = level) updates in DOM, and a large 'Bold graphic' word in mix-blend-mode difference inverts against whatever passes beneath. Sine-driven so the last frame equals the first.
adapt: Swap the painted footage for a same-origin product image, change ink/paper/accent triplets and the 'Bold graphic' word. Keep the full-sine level sweep and the accent band offset (+0.18 to +0.26 above level) — that is the two-tone graphic look.
port: mount(el, shot) adds the canvas, the readout div and the headline inside el. animate returns a timeline with one D-long tween whose onUpdate runs the seek body: repaint footage, per-pixel threshold with lvl = 0.5 + 0.32*sin(2πp), update bar width and percentage text. Scope the #v / #bar lookups to el.
caveats: per-pixel canvas pass every frame, slow to render
mix-blend-mode: difference on the DOM text over a canvas relies on compositing, check in the renderer
procedural footage stands in for real imagery
